sentences: A probabilistic transition system is decisive for a target when it almost surely eventually reaches either the target or states from which the target is unreachable.
This property supports approximation of reachability probabilities in infinite-state models such as probabilistic Petri nets.
The source discusses deciding decisiveness for finite targets and for transition weights that depend on the current marking.
Its own results resolve a substantial dynamic-weight case negatively, proving undecidability for polynomial weights even with finite or upward-closed targets.
The description therefore separates that established limitation from the more specific constant-weight and restricted-model questions motivating the paper.
